faqs.answer: The policy mode calculates scheduled MIP from original contractual amortization. Extra payments shorten actual payoff, which ends modeled coverage, but do not rewrite the original premium schedule.

faqs.question: How does financing the upfront premium change the result?
faqs.answer: The premium increases note principal. The HUD worksheet also applies the financed-upfront adjustment when deriving periodic insurance charges.

sections.title: Reading FHA mortgage cost estimates
paragraphs: FHA loan comparisons should include the supported mortgage-insurance and program-fee assumptions alongside principal and interest. Select the schedule or historical branch that matches the loan details, and review its eligibility notes before interpreting the result. The ownership-cost worksheet can help distinguish the mortgage payment from other housing costs. An estimate does not establish loan eligibility or replace a lender's disclosure.

va-mortgage-calculator.description: Estimate VA purchase or refinance funding fees and payments, using the selected fee tier, financing choice and verified exemption assumptions.

faqs.question: Does the calculator choose a funding-fee tier?
faqs.answer: Verified-policy mode uses the selected loan type, first or later use, down-payment tier and entered verified exemption. It does not independently confirm service eligibility or supporting evidence.

faqs.question: Does VA mortgage insurance add a monthly premium?
faqs.answer: The VA policy mode assigns zero monthly mortgage insurance. The funding fee is a separate upfront charge that can be financed in the scenario.

faqs.question: Does ordinary retirement pay prove a funding-fee exemption?
faqs.answer: No. Select an exemption only when the applicable qualifying status has been verified; receiving retirement pay alone does not establish it.

sections.title: Separating VA loan fees from monthly costs
paragraphs: The VA mortgage calculator separates the financing estimate from supported program-fee assumptions. Review the entered fee treatment and applicable exemption information before comparing scenarios. Financing a fee changes the borrowed balance, while paying it upfront changes cash needed at closing. Use the ownership-cost mode to consider additional recurring housing expenses rather than treating principal and interest as the entire home budget.

down-payment-calculator.description: Calculate down-payment cash, a purchase-price budget or a savings timeline while allowing for entered closing costs.

faqs.question: Is the down payment the only cash needed to buy?
faqs.answer: Not in this model. Estimated closing costs are added to the down payment when calculating the cash needed.

faqs.question: Does the savings timeline include investment growth?
faqs.answer: No. It divides the remaining cash target by monthly savings, without interest, investment returns or changing contributions.

sections.title: Planning the cash needed for a purchase
paragraphs: A down payment can be expressed as a cash amount or a percentage of the purchase price. Use the matching mode depending on which figure you know. The savings timeline helps connect a target with regular contributions. Keep closing costs and any cash reserve separate from the down payment unless the selected fields explicitly include them, so the same money is not counted twice.

house-affordability-calculator.description: Estimate a home-price budget from income and debt limits, or from an entered monthly housing payment allowance.

faqs.question: How do other monthly debts affect the income-based estimate?
faqs.answer: They reduce the amount available under the total debt-to-income limit, which can lower the modeled housing budget.

faqs.question: Does an affordable-price estimate mean a lender will approve it?
faqs.answer: No. Credit history, loan limits, underwriting, local costs and personal spending needs are not fully assessed.

sections.title: Turning a housing budget into a price estimate
paragraphs: Affordability depends on the assumed financing terms and the housing payment available within your budget. Compare the income-based estimate with the mode that starts from a chosen payment. A higher down payment or a different rate can change the estimated purchase price. Treat the result as a planning scenario; it does not confirm that a lender will approve the amount.

rent-calculator.description: Estimate a monthly rent budget from gross income, a chosen spending percentage and the utilities you expect to pay.

faqs.question: Why are utilities deducted from the rent allowance?
faqs.answer: The model treats the chosen income share as a housing budget, then reserves the entered utility amount before estimating rent.

faqs.question: Is the suggested percentage suitable for every household?
faqs.answer: No. Debts, savings goals, household needs and local housing costs can make a percentage rule unsuitable.

sections.title: Building a rent budget around other obligations
paragraphs: Use the rent budget as a starting point for comparing housing choices. The debt-adjusted mode shows how existing monthly obligations affect the amount available under the entered rule. Check which expenses are included before comparing the result with a rental listing. Utilities, transport, and irregular expenses may need their own allowance even when the advertised rent fits the estimate.

debt-ratio-calculator.description: Calculate debt-to-income ratio from gross income and debt payments entered as monthly totals or mixed annual and monthly lines.

faqs.question: Should I use income before or after tax for DTI?
faqs.answer: Use gross income before tax. The mixed-period budget’s spendable-income result is separate from the gross-income denominator used for DTI.

faqs.question: Can I enter annual debt or income amounts?
faqs.answer: Yes. The mixed-period mode normalizes each annual amount to one-twelfth before calculating the ratio.

faqs.question: Does the result establish loan eligibility?
faqs.answer: No. Lenders may count income and obligations differently; use the debts relevant to the comparison.

sections.title: Making income and debt periods comparable
paragraphs: A debt-to-income ratio only makes sense when income and debt payments refer to the same time period. The mixed-period mode helps convert entries before comparing them. Review whether the income figure is gross or take-home pay and use the definition requested by the selected mode. A ratio describes the entered obligations; it does not capture every expense in a household budget.

refinance-calculator.description: Compare refinancing payments, interest and simple break-even, or evaluate payments and remaining debt over the same holding period.

faqs.question: What does simple refinance break-even measure?
faqs.answer: It divides upfront costs by the monthly payment reduction. That payment-only measure does not account for different balances at a later date.

faqs.question: Why compare remaining balances over the same horizon?
faqs.answer: A lower payment can leave more debt outstanding. The horizon mode compares payment differences, upfront net cash and both ending balances together.

sections.title: Comparing refinancing over your own time horizon
paragraphs: A refinance can lower the payment while adding closing costs or extending repayment. Compare the existing and replacement loans over the same period, especially if you expect to move or repay early. The common-horizon mode helps avoid comparing one loan's full lifetime with only part of another. Review the remaining balances together with interest and upfront costs.

For example, 3,000 in upfront costs divided by a 100 monthly payment reduction gives a simple break-even of 30 months. This does not establish total savings: compare the remaining loan balances at the same date, especially when extending the term.

interest-calculator.description: Project compound interest with regular deposits, optional monthly and annual contribution streams, and entered tax and inflation assumptions.

faqs.question: Are monthly and annual contributions alternatives?
faqs.answer: In the dual-stream mode they are additive: the annual contribution is extra to the twelve monthly contributions.

faqs.question: How is tax on interest modeled?
faqs.answer: Tax is applied to positive interest under the stated settlement convention. Account-specific tax treatment and fees are not determined.

faqs.question: Are semimonthly and biweekly compounding the same?
faqs.answer: No. Equivalent nominal rates uses 24 semimonthly periods or 26 biweekly periods per year. It compares equal annual growth, not exact calendar posting dates.

sections.title: Interest after tax and inflation
paragraphs: To isolate interest on a deposit, set Regular contribution to 0. Enter your assumed tax rate and inflation rate to compare the ending balance with its purchasing power. For example, 1,000 at 5% compounded annually for 1 year earns 50 before tax. With 20% tax on interest and 0% inflation, the ending balance is 1,040. Actual account tax rules can differ.

sections.title: Keeping rate and contribution timing consistent
paragraphs: Interest growth depends on the starting balance, the rate convention, and when contributions arrive. Use the mode that matches monthly or annual additions instead of combining them into an unexplained total. When comparing rates, check whether they are nominal or effective. The projection follows the entered rate over time; it does not predict future returns or account for omitted charges.

savings-calculator.description: Estimate savings growth from an opening balance and regular deposits, including contribution timing, tax and inflation scenarios.

faqs.question: Does depositing at the start of a period change the result?
faqs.answer: Yes. Beginning-of-period deposits earn interest for that period; end-of-period deposits begin earning afterward.

faqs.question: Is the inflation-adjusted balance a separate account value?
faqs.answer: No. It expresses the projected nominal balance in purchasing-power terms using the inflation assumption you enter.

sections.title: Build a regular savings plan
paragraphs: Start with the amount already saved, then enter what you can add each month. Compare a lower deposit or a lower rate to see how your plan changes. At 0% interest, an opening balance of 1,000 plus 100 per month for 12 months gives 2,200. Use the monthly + annual contributions mode when you also plan an extra yearly deposit.

sections.title: Separating deposits from savings growth
paragraphs: A savings balance contains both money you contributed and modeled interest. Compare those parts to see how much of the ending value comes from your own deposits. Regular contributions and an initial lump sum have different amounts of time to grow. Keep contribution timing consistent across scenarios, and test a lower rate if you want to understand how dependent a target is on growth.

future-value-calculator.description: Estimate the future value of savings and recurring deposits, including separate monthly and annual contributions and assumed purchasing power.

faqs.question: What is the difference between future value and purchasing power?
faqs.answer: Future value is the projected nominal balance. The inflation-adjusted figure discounts that balance using the assumed change in prices.

faqs.question: Can contributions increase over time?
faqs.answer: The dual-stream mode supports separate increases for monthly and annual contributions. Returns and inflation remain modeled assumptions.

sections.title: Future value of a lump sum
paragraphs: Set Regular contribution to 0 to project a single amount. For example, 10,000 at 5% compounded annually for 10 years becomes 16,288.95 before tax, fees and inflation. Enter a regular contribution to include recurring deposits. The future balance is an amount in future money; use the inflation assumption to also estimate its purchasing power.

sections.title: Reading a future value projection
paragraphs: Future value translates today's balance and planned contributions into a modeled ending amount. It is sensitive to the time horizon, return assumption, and timing of deposits. Compare several plausible inputs rather than interpreting a single projection as a promised balance. Unless the selected calculation explicitly adjusts for inflation, the result is an amount in future money rather than today's purchasing power.

future-value-calculator.seoTitle: Future Value Calculator: Lump Sum & Contributions

cd-calculator.description: Estimate CD-style deposit growth under a fixed rate, compounding schedule and optional tax assumptions, with a projected ending balance.

faqs.question: Can I assume my CD allows recurring deposits?
faqs.answer: No. Some CDs restrict additions. Set recurring contributions to zero unless the actual deposit product permits them.

faqs.question: Does the estimate deduct an early-withdrawal penalty?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. Penalties, promotional terms and product-specific interest rules must be checked against the CD agreement.

sections.title: Interpreting certificate of deposit growth
paragraphs: Use the CD calculator with the deposit, term, and rate convention that match the product you are reviewing. Compare the final balance with the interest earned, rather than treating the entire maturity value as a gain. Check the institution's compounding and withdrawal conditions separately. Early-withdrawal charges or a different credited rate can make actual proceeds differ from the modeled maturity value.

mutual-fund-calculator.description: Project fund contributions and growth, compare entry loads and annual expenses, or estimate a single-lot redemption charge.

faqs.question: How are front-end loads different from ongoing expenses?
faqs.answer: A front load reduces each invested deposit. The expense assumption reduces asset value over time under the modeled settlement schedule.

faqs.question: Does the calculator determine a fund's exit-load rules?
faqs.answer: No. Enter the applicable rate and charge basis from the prospectus; holding periods, waivers and lot treatment are product-specific.

sections.title: Comparing contributions and fund charges
paragraphs: A mutual-fund projection depends on the assumed return and the contributions you make. Use the supported load, expense, or redemption modes to distinguish recurring growth assumptions from specific charges. Keep gross and net return assumptions consistent so that an expense is not deducted twice. A smooth projection illustrates a scenario; actual market returns need not arrive in that sequence.

compound-interest-calculator.description: Project compound growth with regular deposits, then compare equivalent interest rates and contribution schedules.

faqs.question: Why do equivalent nominal rates differ?
faqs.answer: Changing compounding frequency changes the nominal quote needed to preserve the same effective annual growth. The extended rate mode includes 24-period, 26-period and continuous conventions.

faqs.question: Can I add both monthly and yearly deposits?
faqs.answer: Yes. The dual-stream mode adds both streams and allows their annual increase assumptions to be entered separately.

sections.title: Compounding or regular saving?
paragraphs: Use this calculator to explore interest on earlier interest and compare compounding frequencies. For a monthly savings plan, use the Savings Calculator; for purchasing power after tax and inflation, use the Interest Calculator.

sections.title: Understanding compounding and regular deposits
paragraphs: Compound interest applies growth to a balance that already includes earlier interest. Adding regular deposits introduces a separate source of growth, so compare contributed principal with the ending balance. Compounding frequency and deposit frequency describe different events and should not be confused. Use equivalent-rate modes when comparing quoted rates with different conventions, and keep the same time horizon for a fair comparison.

With 1,000 initially, deposits of 100 at each month end, and a 12% nominal annual rate compounded monthly, the balance after 12 months is 2,395.08. Deposits total 2,200 and interest is 195.08. This example assumes no tax, fees or inflation adjustment.

compound-interest-calculator.seoTitle: Compound Interest Calculator with Monthly Deposits

simple-interest-calculator.description: Calculate simple interest and total balance, or solve for missing principal, annual rate or time without compounding.

faqs.question: How does simple interest differ from compound interest?
faqs.answer: Simple interest is calculated only on the original principal. Compound interest also earns interest on previously accumulated interest.

faqs.question: What time unit should I use with the annual rate?
faqs.answer: Use years, including a fractional year when appropriate. The inverse model also treats the rate as an annual rate.

sections.title: When simple interest is the right model
paragraphs: Simple interest uses the original principal for the entered time period, without adding earlier interest to the base. Match the time units to the rate before interpreting the result. The missing-quantity mode can solve for an unknown input when the other values are known. Do not use a simple-interest result as a substitute for a loan schedule that compounds or reduces principal through payments.

finance-calculator.description: Solve time-value-of-money problems for present value, future value, payment, rate or periods, with explicit cash-flow conventions.

faqs.question: Why are some cash-flow entries negative?
faqs.answer: In signed TVM mode, payments made and money received have opposite signs. The savings mode instead uses positive contributions.

faqs.question: Does payment timing affect the answer?
faqs.answer: Yes. A beginning-of-period payment has one additional period of growth or discounting compared with an end-of-period payment.

sections.title: Understanding cash-flow signs and timing
paragraphs: Time-value-of-money calculations connect present value, future value, periodic payments, and interest. In the signed cash-flow mode, money paid out and money received use opposite signs. An unexpected negative result may therefore describe cash-flow direction rather than a loss. Check whether payments occur at the beginning or end of each period before comparing the answer with another financial model.

investment-calculator.description: Explore investment targets, required contributions and assumed returns, including signed TVM and separate monthly and annual deposit scenarios.

faqs.question: Does solving for a return predict what an investment will earn?
faqs.answer: No. It finds the constant modeled return needed to connect the entered cash flows and target; it is not a forecast.

faqs.question: Which mode should I use for extra yearly contributions?
faqs.answer: Use Monthly + annual contributions when a yearly deposit is additional to the monthly savings stream.

sections.title: Testing investment assumptions separately
paragraphs: Change one assumption at a time when comparing investment projections: the starting balance, contribution amount, return, or horizon. This makes it easier to see what drives the difference. The signed cash-flow and equivalent-rate modes answer more specific financing questions. A constant-rate projection smooths away market fluctuations, so use it to explore scenarios rather than to predict a guaranteed account value.

present-value-calculator.description: Discount a future lump sum and regular payments to today's value, with payment-frequency and beginning-or-end timing options.

faqs.question: Why does a higher discount rate reduce present value?
faqs.answer: Future payments are divided by larger growth factors, so their equivalent value today becomes smaller.

faqs.question: Are annual and monthly payments treated the same way?
faqs.answer: No. The timing mode converts the effective annual rate to the selected payment interval and uses the corresponding number of periods.

sections.title: Choosing the discount rate and payment timing
paragraphs: Present value expresses future money as an equivalent amount at the selected discount rate. A future lump sum and a stream of payments require different inputs. Check the payment frequency and whether payments arrive at the start or end of a period. The discount rate is an assumption you supply; changing it can materially change the value assigned to the same future cash flows.

interest-rate-calculator.description: Find the implied fixed annual loan rate from a principal balance, monthly payment and repayment term, excluding financing fees.

faqs.question: Is the solved interest rate the same as APR?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. This mode excludes fees and irregular payment dates, so it solves an implied rate rather than a fee-inclusive APR.

faqs.question: What if the payment is too small for the entered term?
faqs.answer: The inputs may not support a nonnegative amortizing rate. Review the principal, payment and term instead of treating an invalid scenario as a quote.

sections.title: Interpreting an implied interest rate
paragraphs: An implied rate is the rate that reconciles the entered balance, payment, and term under the displayed model. It is not automatically a lender's disclosed annual percentage rate, because fee treatment and timing may differ. Verify the payment frequency and amounts before solving. Small differences in a payment or remaining term can change the rate needed to make the figures consistent.

apr-calculator.description: Estimate a loan's fee-inclusive borrowing rate by comparing net proceeds with scheduled payments and selected payment frequencies.

faqs.question: Why can APR exceed the stated interest rate?
faqs.answer: Upfront financing charges reduce the cash received while scheduled repayments remain based on the loan, increasing the modeled borrowing rate.

faqs.question: Is this a legally compliant APR disclosure for every loan?
faqs.answer: No. Required fees, timing conventions and disclosure rules vary. This is a stated cash-flow estimate, not a jurisdiction-specific disclosure.

sections.title: Comparing interest rates with borrowing costs
paragraphs: APR calculations connect the cash received with the payments and supported fees over time. A stated interest rate can differ from a fee-adjusted borrowing rate. Enter fees according to the selected mode and compare offers with consistent payment timing. The result follows the calculator's assumptions; use the lender's required disclosure when a legal or contractual APR definition is needed.

inflation-calculator.description: Compare US purchasing power with versioned BLS CPI-U data, or explore future price changes using an inflation rate you choose.

faqs.question: Does the historical mode use my assumed inflation rate?
faqs.answer: No. It uses the included BLS CPI-U series. Your chosen constant rate applies only to the forward scenario.

faqs.question: Why is a historical month unavailable?
faqs.answer: The tool only uses published data included in its versioned dataset. Missing observations are not replaced with guessed CPI values.

sections.title: Historical purchasing power versus a scenario
paragraphs: The historical inflation mode uses the stated US CPI series and supported dates. The scenario mode instead applies an inflation rate that you choose. Keep these purposes separate: a scenario is not a forecast from the historical dataset. Compare the amount in its original date's money with the equivalent amount at the target date to understand the change in purchasing power.

annuity-payout-calculator.description: Estimate a fixed withdrawal from savings or how long a balance lasts under a constant return and monthly drawdown scenario.

faqs.question: Does this estimate a lifetime insurance annuity payment?
faqs.answer: No. It models withdrawals from a balance. Insurer pricing, mortality, guarantees and contract fees are outside the calculation.

faqs.question: Why can the projected balance last longer at a higher return?
faqs.answer: More assumed growth offsets withdrawals. Actual returns vary, so a constant-return result does not guarantee the balance will last that long.

sections.title: Balancing withdrawals with account duration
paragraphs: An annuity payout estimate links an opening balance, assumed growth, and a withdrawal schedule. Use the duration mode when the payment is known, or the payment mode when a target duration is known. Check whether withdrawals occur at the beginning or end of each period. A constant-return account projection does not reproduce every feature or guarantee of an insurance annuity contract.

annuity-calculator.description: Estimate the future value of an initial balance and equal recurring contributions under a constant-return annuity model.

faqs.question: What does annuity mean in this calculator?
faqs.answer: It means a regular stream of equal cash flows. The result is not a quote for an insurance annuity product.

faqs.question: Are fees and insurance guarantees included?
faqs.answer: No. The calculation covers the entered cash flows and return assumptions, without mortality pricing, product guarantees or contract charges.

sections.title: Accumulating a stream of contributions
paragraphs: An annuity accumulation calculation models a sequence of contributions growing over time. Earlier contributions usually remain invested for more periods than later ones, so timing matters. Compare the total contributed with the ending balance and keep the payment schedule aligned with the selected mode. Contract charges, changing returns, or withdrawals need explicit treatment before this becomes a model of a particular annuity product.

retirement-calculator.description: Model retirement savings, salary-based contributions and inflation-linked spending, with a year-by-year withdrawal scenario.

faqs.question: Does an income-based retirement need use my final salary?
faqs.answer: In Salary growth & income-based retirement, the need is a share of current income, inflated to retirement once. Savings based on salary grow separately with each year’s modeled income.

faqs.question: What does a negative projected retirement balance mean?
faqs.answer: It marks spending the modeled resources cannot fund. It is not a prediction that an investment account can continue making those withdrawals.

faqs.question: Does the target include market volatility?
faqs.answer: No. Constant return assumptions do not model volatility or sequence-of-returns risk.

sections.title: Connecting a retirement target with savings
paragraphs: Start by distinguishing the balance you want at retirement from the income you want after retiring. The available modes connect savings, salary-based contributions, withdrawals, and duration under their stated assumptions. Check how inflation is handled before comparing future amounts with today's spending. Testing several contribution and return assumptions can show which parts of the plan depend most on uncertain inputs.

401k-calculator.description: Project 401(k)-style savings, salary-based deferrals and tiered employer matching, with optional frozen 2026 caps and withdrawal estimates.

faqs.question: Are contribution limits always applied to the projection?
faqs.answer: No. The salary-based mode offers uncapped scenarios or frozen 2026 limits. Future limits and plan eligibility are not predicted.

faqs.question: How are employer matching tiers applied?
faqs.answer: Each tier matches the employee contribution slice up to its cumulative salary threshold. Contributions and the match enter at year end.

faqs.question: How does the dated distribution mode handle the additional tax?
faqs.answer: It tests age 59½, the specified employer-plan separation-year rule and entered verified exceptions against the taxable portion. An exception to additional tax does not remove ordinary income tax.

sections.title: Reviewing contributions, matching, and withdrawals
paragraphs: A 401(k) projection can separate your contributions from employer matching and investment growth. Review the salary and matching inputs before interpreting the ending balance. Withdrawal modes answer different questions from accumulation and include only the supported tax assumptions. A regional display preference does not change this tool's US account rules, and the projection does not verify the terms of your employer's plan.

ira-calculator.description: Explore IRA growth and withdrawals, compare traditional and Roth savings from equal pretax resources, or estimate a 2026 contribution ceiling.

faqs.question: Does the IRA ceiling determine deductibility or full eligibility?
faqs.answer: No. It compares eligible compensation with the age-based combined ceiling, before MAGI restrictions, deductibility and other eligibility rules.

faqs.question: What does an equal pretax-budget comparison change?
faqs.answer: It reduces the Roth contribution by the assumed current tax, then compares it with traditional savings after the assumed withdrawal tax.

faqs.question: Does leaving an employer at age 55 create an IRA exception?
faqs.answer: The dated mode applies its separation-year exception only to the relevant qualified employer plan, not to an IRA. Other exceptions must be separately established.

sections.title: Keeping IRA contribution and tax assumptions aligned
paragraphs: The IRA modes cover different planning questions, including account growth, contribution ceilings, and supported distributions. Select the branch that matches the tax year and account scenario before entering values. The equal-budget comparison is useful when tax treatment changes how much can be contributed from the same pretax resources. Read the mode's limitations before using an estimate in a tax or withdrawal decision.

roth-ira-calculator.description: Compare Roth, traditional and taxable scenarios using qualified-distribution assumptions, equal pretax resources and a separate 2026 ceiling.

faqs.question: Why is Roth growth treated as tax-free in the comparison?
faqs.answer: The scenario assumes qualified distributions. It does not establish contribution eligibility or decide whether an actual withdrawal qualifies.

faqs.question: Why can equal pretax resources mean a smaller Roth contribution?
faqs.answer: Roth funding uses after-tax money in this model, so the entered current tax reduces the amount invested from the same pretax budget.

faqs.question: Does the 2026 ceiling account for every income restriction?
faqs.answer: No. It is an age-and-compensation ceiling before MAGI restrictions, deductibility and other eligibility rules.

sections.title: Comparing accounts from the same starting budget
paragraphs: A Roth IRA comparison is most informative when both alternatives begin with a consistent budget. A contribution made from after-tax money is not directly comparable with a larger pretax contribution without accounting for that difference. Use the equal-budget mode for that question, and review the supported contribution-ceiling assumptions separately. The model does not predict future tax rules or investment performance.

pension-calculator.description: Compare pension present values, lump sums and single-life or joint-survivor payment streams using explicit timing and lifetime assumptions.

faqs.question: What does the pension present value represent?
faqs.answer: It discounts the modeled payments over the entered horizon. It is not a guaranteed transfer value or an insurer's quote.

faqs.question: Does the survivor comparison predict either person's lifespan?
faqs.answer: No. The cash-flow streams use the lifetime assumptions you enter. They compare scenarios rather than probabilities of surviving to particular ages.

sections.title: Comparing pension payment streams
paragraphs: Pension choices can differ in starting date, payment amount, and survivor benefits. Compare the timing of those streams as well as their present value under the selected discount rate. A later start may change the payment without making every scenario equivalent. The calculation values the entered streams; it does not determine personal longevity or establish which pension election best fits a household.

rmd-calculator.description: Estimate owner RMDs with distribution-year rules, applicable lifetime tables and return-based projections, within the stated account scope.

faqs.question: Which balance and table does the calendar mode use?
faqs.answer: Enter the prior December 31 balance. It uses the Uniform Lifetime Table or the Joint table when the entered sole-beneficiary spouse is more than ten years younger and within the verified dataset.

faqs.question: Does this determine a first distribution year?
faqs.answer: Calendar mode reports one for supported birth cohorts and account assumptions, with first-year deadline information. It stops for policy verification on the unresolved 1959 cohort.

faqs.question: Does a zero owner RMD mean every withdrawal rule is satisfied?
faqs.answer: No. Owner Roth exemptions and eligible current-employer deferral are limited branches. Inherited accounts and other account-specific obligations are outside this model.

sections.title: Using the right balance and distribution year
paragraphs: A required minimum distribution estimate depends on the applicable year, balance, and supported life-expectancy table. Review the owner-calendar mode when timing matters, rather than treating every calendar year as identical. Keep the account balance date consistent with the field instructions. The tool covers the owner scenarios described in its notes and should not be assumed to handle every inherited-account rule.

social-security-calculator.description: Compare Social Security claiming ages, full-retirement-age cohorts and two benefit streams under shared COLA and discount assumptions.

faqs.question: Where does the starting benefit come from?
faqs.answer: Enter an FRA benefit from your SSA estimate or supply the two scenario benefits. The calculator does not reconstruct benefits from your earnings history.

faqs.question: What is held constant in a two-stream comparison?
faqs.answer: Both streams use a common valuation age, lifespan, COLA and discount assumption. Candidate-age rows use the entered FRA benefit even when the two comparison amounts are supplied manually.

faqs.question: Does waiting beyond age 70 add delayed credits?
faqs.answer: No. The model caps age-based delayed credits at 70; later changes in an actual benefit can have other causes.

sections.title: Comparing benefit streams across claiming ages
paragraphs: A claiming-age comparison combines the assumed benefit with the age when payments begin. A larger monthly benefit can start later, so compare cumulative streams as well as individual payments. Use the birth-cohort mode to check the supported full-retirement-age assumption. The calculator models the benefit figures you enter and does not retrieve an official earnings record or guarantee an award amount.

college-cost-calculator.description: Project college costs and a chosen funded share, then estimate monthly savings with optional annual tax on investment interest.

faqs.question: Does the model assume savings keep growing during college?
faqs.answer: No. It aims to hold all modeled nominal study costs at enrollment and assumes no investment gains during the study years.

faqs.question: How does the taxable-savings mode apply tax?
faqs.answer: It taxes positive accumulated interest at each saving year-end. Monthly contributions are not interest, and the model does not establish 529 or other account tax eligibility.

faqs.question: How do I model partial funding?
faqs.answer: Enter the share of projected costs to fund from these savings. Scholarships, grants and financial-aid awards are not selected automatically.

sections.title: Matching college savings with expected costs
paragraphs: College planning combines a current cost estimate, time until enrollment, cost growth, and savings contributions. Review how much of the projected expense is funded rather than looking only at the account balance. A change in the inflation assumption affects the target, while the investment return affects savings growth. The taxable-savings mode includes only its stated tax treatment, not every education-account rule.

debt-payoff-calculator.description: Compare avalanche and snowball debt repayment schedules, with fixed minimum payments and extra cash rolled into remaining balances.

faqs.question: How do avalanche and snowball ordering differ?
faqs.answer: Avalanche prioritizes higher interest rates; snowball prioritizes smaller balances. Both pay entered minimums before allocating extra cash.

faqs.question: What happens after one debt is paid off?
faqs.answer: Its freed payment is redirected to remaining debts. The model assumes no new borrowing and fixed minimum-payment amounts until payoff.

sections.title: Comparing payoff priorities with the same budget
paragraphs: Keep the total payment budget constant when comparing debt-payoff strategies. Otherwise, a faster result may come from paying more rather than changing which debt receives extra money first. Check how minimum payments, rollover amounts, and dated extras are entered. The schedule assumes the modeled debts and rates, so new borrowing or a rate change requires an updated scenario.

credit-card-payoff-calculator.description: Plan payoff across multiple credit cards using avalanche or snowball ordering, entered minimum payments and a monthly extra-payment budget.

faqs.question: Does the schedule recalculate card minimums as balances fall?
faqs.answer: No. Entered minimum payments remain fixed until payoff, unlike issuer formulas that may change the minimum each statement.

faqs.question: Does monthly APR divided by 12 match every card statement?
faqs.answer: No. This schedule uses that monthly approximation; daily interest methods, fees, rate changes and new purchases can produce different statement amounts.

sections.title: Planning payments across multiple cards
paragraphs: Enter each card balance and rate separately so that the payoff schedule can allocate payments to the correct debt. Compare strategies using the same overall budget and review what happens when a cleared card's payment rolls over. A statement's changing minimum-payment rules may differ from the model. Adding purchases during repayment also changes the balance path shown by the estimate.

debt-consolidation-calculator.description: Compare current debt obligations with a consolidation loan, including financed fees, the new payment and repayment-term effects.

faqs.question: Are consolidation fees added to the new loan?
faqs.answer: The modeled financed fees are added to the combined debt balance before calculating the new loan payment.

faqs.question: Is a lower monthly payment necessarily a cheaper consolidation?
faqs.answer: No. A longer repayment term can reduce payments while increasing total interest. Compare fees, interest and time in debt together.

sections.title: Checking whether consolidation reduces total cost
paragraphs: Consolidation replaces several payment streams with a new borrowing arrangement. Compare the new term, fees, and total repayment with the existing debts, not just the first monthly payment. A longer term may make the payment smaller while keeping debt outstanding for longer. Use the fee-adjusted comparison to see how supported upfront charges affect the apparent savings.

student-loan-calculator.description: Model standard student-loan repayment or annual borrowing during school, with explicit delay-interest and capitalization choices.

faqs.question: Is unpaid school interest always added to principal?
faqs.answer: In the school-borrowing mode, it stays separate unless hypothetical capitalization is selected. The standard deferment mode uses its stated one-time capitalization assumption.

faqs.question: Does this determine federal income-driven payments or forgiveness?
faqs.answer: No. Interest treatment is a scenario choice, not an inference about program eligibility. Income-driven plans and forgiveness require current program-specific guidance.

faqs.question: When is new school borrowing assumed to occur?
faqs.answer: The model adds the annual borrowing at the start of each school year, then tracks each amount over its time outstanding.

sections.title: Separating school borrowing from repayment
paragraphs: Borrowing during school and repaying an existing student loan are different stages. Choose the mode that matches the balance and timing you know. The repayment-budget mode works backward from a payment, while fixed-payment payoff estimates how long a balance takes to clear. These scenarios follow the stated loan model and do not automatically reproduce income-based repayment or forgiveness programs.

bond-calculator.description: Calculate regular-coupon bond price or yield, including dated settlement, accrued interest and selectable day-count conventions.

faqs.question: Is accrued interest included in the bond price?
faqs.answer: The dated mode reports clean price, accrued interest and dirty price separately. Its cash settlement amount includes accrued interest. The basic years-to-maturity mode assumes coupon-date valuation.

faqs.question: Why does the day-count convention change the answer?
faqs.answer: The convention determines the accrued portion of a coupon and the time to the next payment. US-NASD and European 30/360 can differ at month ends.

faqs.question: Does the yield account for default or early redemption?
faqs.answer: No. These modes assume the scheduled regular coupons and redemption amount are paid.

sections.title: Reading bond price and yield together
paragraphs: A bond's coupon rate, market price, and yield describe different things. When working with settlement dates, check the payment schedule and day-count convention because accrued interest and remaining cash flows depend on them. Compare clean and settlement-related values using the labels shown. A calculated yield assumes the modeled payments and does not remove the possibility of default or changing market prices.

average-return-calculator.description: Compare arithmetic and geometric period returns, or estimate annual money-weighted return from dated deposits and receipts.

faqs.question: Which average reflects compound growth across equal periods?
faqs.answer: The geometric average links the period growth factors. The arithmetic average adds percentage returns and divides by their count.

faqs.question: What if my deposits and withdrawals occur on irregular dates?
faqs.answer: Use the dated money-weighted mode with negative investor payments and positive receipts. It accounts for unequal intervals using elapsed days.

sections.title: Choosing an average that matches the question
paragraphs: An arithmetic average summarizes individual period returns, while a compounded result describes growth across periods. Deposits and withdrawals introduce another question: the return on money invested at different times. Use the dated money-weighted mode for that cash-flow perspective. Two accounts can have the same sequence of market returns but different investor outcomes when their contributions occur at different dates.

roi-calculator.description: Calculate ROI and annualized return from a holding period or exact dates, or use dated cash flows for money-weighted return.

faqs.question: How does exact-date annualized ROI handle time?
faqs.answer: It uses the actual elapsed calendar days and a 365-day annualization convention between the initial cost and final proceeds.

faqs.question: Which mode fits several deposits and withdrawals?
faqs.answer: Use dated money-weighted return with signed cash flows. Simple ROI annualization assumes one initial investment and one final receipt.

sections.title: Putting return on investment in context
paragraphs: ROI compares the gain or loss with the amount invested, but a percentage alone does not describe how long the investment lasted. Use the exact-date annualized mode when duration matters. If money enters or leaves at several dates, the dated cash-flow mode is more informative than treating everything as one initial purchase. Keep costs consistent across investments being compared.

irr-calculator.description: Estimate periodic or dated internal rates of return, including recurring cash-flow scenarios and detected multiple solutions.

faqs.question: Is every IRR result automatically an annual rate?
faqs.answer: No. Periodic IRR uses the cash-flow interval. Dated IRR uses elapsed days with a 365-day annualization convention; recurring mode also shows annual conversion.

faqs.question: Can the same cash flows have more than one IRR?
faqs.answer: Yes. Multiple sign changes can create multiple roots. The calculator reports detected solutions within its supported search range.

sections.title: Reading an internal rate of return carefully
paragraphs: IRR is the rate that makes the modeled cash flows balance in present-value terms. Enter outgoing and incoming amounts with the required signs, and select periodic or dated cash flows according to their timing. Irregular sign changes can make interpretation more difficult. Compare the cash-flow schedule and investment size alongside the rate rather than ranking projects from IRR alone.

payback-period-calculator.description: Estimate simple or discounted payback from entered periodic cash flows or an annual return stream with assumed growth.

faqs.question: How is a fractional payback period calculated?
faqs.answer: The model interpolates cash within the recovery period. Actual receipts arriving only at period end can produce a different practical recovery date.

faqs.question: Does the shortest payback always identify the best investment?
faqs.answer: No. Payback alone does not value all later cash flows or fully describe risk. Discounted payback also depends on the chosen discount rate.

sections.title: What a payback period does and does not show
paragraphs: The payback period identifies when accumulated modeled inflows recover the initial outlay. Check whether the selected result uses discounted cash flows before comparing it with another payback estimate. Cash received after the recovery point still matters to total project value. A short payback therefore describes recovery speed, rather than proving that a project has the highest overall return.

depreciation-calculator.description: Compare book-depreciation schedules, including fiscal dates, partial-year conventions and an optional switch to straight-line expense.

faqs.question: Is this a complete tax-depreciation calculation?
faqs.answer: No. These are book-depreciation scenarios. MACRS, bonus depreciation and section 179 eligibility are not determined.

faqs.question: What does the fiscal-year mode add?
faqs.answer: It accepts a service date, fiscal-year start, declining factor and partial-year convention. It can switch permanently to straight-line when that gives the higher annual rate.

faqs.question: Will every declining-balance schedule reach salvage value?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. With the straight-line switch disabled, the model leaves unused basis rather than forcing a final writeoff.

sections.title: Allocating asset cost across accounting periods
paragraphs: Book depreciation spreads the depreciable amount across periods according to the selected method. Enter the asset cost, residual value, and useful life consistently, and use the fiscal-year mode when the acquisition date affects the schedule. The remaining book value is an accounting result rather than a prediction of resale price. Tax depreciation can follow separate rules from the displayed book schedule.

margin-calculator.description: Calculate profit margin and markup, solve a target selling price, or explore simplified stock and currency margin requirements.

faqs.question: Why are margin and markup different percentages?
faqs.answer: Margin divides profit by revenue; markup divides profit by cost. The profit-and-margin inverse requires positive profit and positive margin in this model.

faqs.question: Do the stock and FX modes apply my broker’s exact requirements?
faqs.answer: No. They use entered ratios, leverage and exchange rates. Broker rules, financing charges and instrument requirements can differ.

sections.title: Distinguishing profit margin from markup
paragraphs: Profit margin compares profit with the selling price, while markup compares it with cost. Confusing the denominator can produce a price that misses the intended margin. Use the missing-cost or missing-price mode when working backward from a target. The stock and foreign-exchange margin modes answer separate collateral questions and should not be interpreted as product-pricing calculations.

commission-calculator.description: Calculate flat or tiered sales commission, total compensation, or the sales and rate needed for a target commission.

faqs.question: Do tiered rates apply to all sales once a threshold is reached?
faqs.answer: No. This is a marginal schedule: each rate applies only to sales within its tier, rather than retroactively to all sales.

faqs.question: What happens above the highest entered tier?
faqs.answer: The final tier's rate continues above its upper limit. Confirm that this matches the actual commission agreement.

sections.title: Understanding flat and tiered commission
paragraphs: A flat commission applies one rate to the selected sales amount. A marginal tier schedule applies different rates to portions of that amount, rather than automatically applying the highest rate to all sales. Enter the tiers in the order requested and compare the total commission with the underlying sales figure. The result follows the entered schedule, not an employer's unentered bonus or clawback rules.

discount-calculator.description: Calculate sale price and savings, combine a percentage and fixed reduction, or recover the original price from a known pair.

faqs.question: In what order are a percentage and fixed discount applied?
faqs.answer: The main calculation applies the percentage reduction first, then subtracts the fixed amount. The known-pair mode solves one discount relationship from the selected inputs.

faqs.question: Can a zero final price determine the original price?
faqs.answer: At 100% off, every original price produces zero. That inverse case is indeterminate; a positive final price with 100% off is inconsistent.

faqs.question: Is sales tax included in the discounted price?
faqs.answer: No. This tool does not decide how a discount or coupon affects the taxable amount.

sections.title: Checking the price before and after a discount
paragraphs: Choose the discount mode based on which two values you already know. A reduction amount, a percentage, and a final price describe related but different quantities. Check that the original price is the comparison base before interpreting the percentage saved. Taxes, delivery charges, and other fees need separate consideration if they are not part of the entered price.

percent-off-calculator.description: Calculate percent-off savings and final prices, or combine two successive percentage discounts without simply adding them.

faqs.question: Do discounts of 20% and then 10% equal 30% off?
faqs.answer: No. Each percentage acts on the current price, so a $100 item falls to $80 and then $72, for a 28% combined reduction.

faqs.question: Can I recover an original price from the sale price?
faqs.answer: Use the known-pair mode with final price and percent off. A zero final price at 100% off cannot identify one original price.

sections.title: Why successive discounts do not simply add
paragraphs: A second percentage discount normally applies to the price remaining after the first reduction. Use the consecutive-discount mode to see that effect rather than adding the two percentages. The known-pair mode can work backward from a final price or saving. Keep the original price visible when comparing promotions so that a larger advertised percentage is not mistaken for a lower final cost.

sales-tax-calculator.description: Calculate net price, sales tax, gross price or an implied tax rate from a selected pair of known values.

faqs.question: How do I remove tax already included in a total?
faqs.answer: Divide the total by one plus the tax rate. The known-pair mode also solves from net and gross prices or from tax amount and a positive rate.

faqs.question: Does the calculator find the sales-tax rate for my address?
faqs.answer: No. You supply the rate and determine whether the transaction is taxable or exempt.

sections.title: Working with tax-inclusive and pre-tax prices
paragraphs: The sales-tax modes distinguish a pre-tax amount from a price that already includes tax. Choose the known pair that matches your receipt or estimate so that tax is not added twice. Enter the applicable rate yourself; selecting a display currency does not supply a local tax rate. The result follows that rate and does not decide whether a transaction is taxable.

vat-calculator.description: Calculate VAT, net or gross amounts, or an implied VAT rate from the values you already know.

faqs.question: How is VAT extracted from a tax-inclusive price?
faqs.answer: Net equals gross divided by one plus the entered rate. VAT is the difference. The known-pair mode can also start from tax amount and a positive rate.

faqs.question: Does this decide which VAT rate or exemption applies?
faqs.answer: No. Rate selection, place of supply, exemptions and recoverability are outside this arithmetic model.

sections.title: Extracting VAT from an inclusive price
paragraphs: When a price already includes VAT, the tax component must be separated from the total using the inclusive-price relationship. Multiplying the inclusive total by the rate would use the wrong base. Select the known-pair mode that matches the figures available. The calculator performs the arithmetic for an entered rate and does not establish registration, exemption, or input-tax recovery eligibility.

salary-calculator.description: Convert gross salary across hourly through annual pay periods, including quarterly pay, and compare unpaid-day adjustments.

faqs.question: Why do biweekly and semimonthly pay differ?
faqs.answer: Annualization uses 26 biweekly periods and 24 semimonthly periods. Quarterly pay uses four periods.

faqs.question: Do holidays and vacation automatically reduce annual salary?
faqs.answer: Only the separate unpaid-day scenario reduces earnings. Paid leave does not automatically reduce a fixed annual salary.

faqs.question: Is the converted salary my take-home pay?
faqs.answer: No. These are gross-pay conversions before taxes, benefits and payroll deductions.

sections.title: Comparing pay across different periods
paragraphs: An hourly, monthly, and annual salary comparison depends on the work schedule assumed. Check working days, hours, and nonworking days before comparing offers. A simple period conversion does not automatically account for overtime, variable shifts, benefits, or tax withholding. Use the pay-period mode when the calendar or number of paid periods is central to the question.

budget-calculator.description: Build a monthly budget from take-home totals or mixed-period gross-income lines, with pretax savings, assumed tax and debt payments.

faqs.question: Should I enter gross salary or take-home income?
faqs.answer: Use take-home income in the simple budget. In Mixed-period budget & debt ratio, use gross income; that mode separately subtracts pretax saving and the entered flat tax.

faqs.question: Can I combine annual and monthly amounts?
faqs.answer: Yes. Each mixed-period line has its own annual or monthly selector; annual amounts are divided by twelve.

faqs.question: How can I avoid counting a debt payment twice?
faqs.answer: Enter a payment in either living expenses or debt payments, not both. The mixed-period model deducts the two groups separately.

sections.title: Making a monthly budget from mixed expenses
paragraphs: Convert income and expenses to a common period before comparing the totals. A yearly bill can be easy to miss in a monthly budget unless an allowance is made for it. Review the remaining balance after recurring obligations, then consider irregular spending separately. The mixed-period mode helps align timing; it does not know about transactions that have not been entered.

tax-calculator.description: Explore US federal ordinary-income tax and separate 2026 self-employment, investment-income, credit and AMT worksheets.

faqs.question: Does this produce one complete federal tax result?
faqs.answer: No. The ordinary-income, self-employment, investment-income, credit and AMT modules are separate bounded worksheets. Some totals overlap, so do not add every displayed metric together.

faqs.question: Which years and income rules are covered?
faqs.answer: The detailed ordinary-income mode offers 2025 and 2026. Other modes state their own scope; qualified-gain, dependent-credit and AMT branches exclude the special cases listed with their results.

faqs.question: Does the dependent-credit worksheet establish eligibility?
faqs.answer: No. Eligibility is supplied as an assumption. The basic refundable branch is limited to at most two qualifying children and excludes the special Schedule 8812 branches.

sections.title: Selecting the correct US tax worksheet
paragraphs: Start with the tax year and the specific income, deduction, or credit question you need to model. The calculator contains separate supported branches, so a result from one worksheet should not be assumed to represent an entire return. Review eligibility and limitation notes beside the selected mode. Changing the website language or currency does not convert these US federal rules into another country's tax system.

take-home-pay-calculator.description: Estimate take-home wages, 2026 W-4 federal withholding and paycheck FICA, with separate wage bases and year-to-date inputs.

faqs.question: Can I estimate withholding for one paycheck?
faqs.answer: Yes. The W-4 mode uses taxable wages for that pay, pay frequency and the entered W-4 Step 2, 3 and 4 amounts. It is separate from the annual wage-tax estimate.

faqs.question: Are gross wages and payroll-tax wages always identical?
faqs.answer: No. Federal withholding, Social Security and Medicare can use different taxable wage amounts. Enter the wage base requested by each mode.

faqs.question: Does Additional Medicare withholding use my filing status?
faqs.answer: The paycheck FICA branch uses the employer’s $200,000 withholding trigger. Final Additional Medicare liability uses a separate filing-status calculation.

sections.title: Separating tax liability from paycheck withholding
paragraphs: An annual tax estimate and withholding from a particular paycheck are related but different calculations. Choose the mode that matches the pay period, wage base, and deduction treatment you want to examine. Compare gross pay, deductions, and the resulting net amount using consistent timing. The supported federal calculations do not automatically include every state, local, employer, or benefit-plan adjustment.

marriage-calculator.description: Compare 2025 or 2026 ordinary-income tax for two eligible single-filer scenarios and one joint scenario, with selected deductions.

faqs.question: What does the year-based comparison include?
faqs.answer: It compares the selected year’s ordinary-income brackets using basic standard deductions or the deduction amounts you enter.

faqs.question: Does it decide whether a married couple should file separately?
faqs.answer: No. It compares two eligible single-filer scenarios with one joint scenario. Married-filing-separately rules, credits and other taxes require a separate analysis.

sections.title: Comparing filing scenarios consistently
paragraphs: A marriage-tax comparison needs the same underlying incomes and supported deductions in both scenarios. Review the year and filing assumptions before interpreting the difference. A change in total modeled tax is not a complete measure of the financial effects of marriage. Credits, eligibility rules, and income types outside the selected branch may require a more complete return calculation.

estate-tax-calculator.description: Estimate a 2026 federal estate-tax scenario from asset and deduction lines, adjusted gifts, exclusion and entered credit assumptions.

faqs.question: Do both estate modes use only a flat 40% rate?
faqs.answer: No. The legacy approximation uses the top rate above its entered exclusion. The detailed assets-and-gifts mode uses the graduated tentative-tax schedule and applicable exclusion credit.

faqs.question: Can I enter a deceased spouse’s unused exclusion?
faqs.answer: The detailed mode accepts a valid elected DSUE amount as an assumption. It does not determine portability eligibility or make the required election.

faqs.question: Are state inheritance taxes and all gift adjustments included?
faqs.answer: State and generation-skipping taxes are excluded. Adjusted taxable gifts, gift tax payable, deductions and other credits must be supplied after separate verification.

sections.title: Understanding a modeled taxable estate
paragraphs: The estate worksheet starts from the entered assets, adjustments, gifts, and supported credits. Keep estate value separate from the amount potentially subject to tax under the selected federal assumptions. The result is a planning estimate for the stated year and scope. It does not determine asset ownership, valuation disputes, state estate or inheritance taxes, or the effect of an unmodeled trust arrangement.

rental-property-calculator.description: Estimate rental cash flow and returns, or model a holding period with growing expenses, mortgage payoff and sale proceeds.

faqs.question: Should mortgage payments be included in operating expenses?
faqs.answer: No. Operating expenses exclude debt service and depreciation. The model deducts mortgage payments separately when calculating cash flow.

faqs.question: How does a sale affect holding-period return?
faqs.answer: Final cash flow includes the sale proceeds after selling costs and remaining mortgage debt. It is counted once in the investor-return stream.

sections.title: Comparing rental cash flow with sale proceeds
paragraphs: Rental income, operating costs, financing, and eventual sale proceeds affect different parts of an investment's return. Review ongoing cash flow separately from the holding-period result. An attractive sale assumption can hide weak annual cash flow, while a positive monthly figure may omit costs not entered. Compare scenarios using consistent vacancy, expense, financing, and holding-period assumptions.

rent-vs-buy-calculator.description: Compare renting and buying through housing cash flows, refundable deposits, mortgage equity and a common investment-return assumption.

faqs.question: How does the detailed mode treat a refundable deposit?
faqs.answer: It records the deposit as an upfront renter outflow and the selected refund at exit. A full refund removes its nominal cost but can still have a present-value opportunity cost.

faqs.question: Is mortgage principal counted as an expense twice?
faqs.answer: No. The detailed mode includes payments in cash outflows and subtracts remaining loan debt from sale proceeds to calculate equity at exit.

faqs.question: What does the terminal buying advantage measure?
faqs.answer: In the detailed mode it grows the same present-value cost difference to the comparison end date. It is not an additional benefit to add to that difference.

sections.title: Making a rent-or-buy comparison over one horizon
paragraphs: A rent-versus-buy result depends on how long you stay and what happens to housing costs, property value, and alternative savings. Compare both paths over the same horizon and review the treatment of deposits and ending equity. A refundable deposit is different from an expense. The model is especially sensitive to long-term assumptions, so test several scenarios before relying on a single break-even point.

currency-calculator.description: Convert currencies with an entered rate or dated ECB daily reference rates, keeping transaction fees and bank spreads separate.

faqs.question: Are ECB reference rates live transaction quotes?
faqs.answer: No. They are dated informational reference rates. Banks and payment providers may use different rates, spreads, fees or settlement times.

faqs.question: Are my amount and currency choices sent to the rate provider?
faqs.answer: No. The site fetches a generic reference-rate feed; your selected currencies and amount are used for conversion in the browser.

sections.title: Reading an exchange-rate result
paragraphs: Select the conversion mode according to whether you want an entered rate, a dated reference rate, or a supported spot quote. Check the source and timestamp shown with the result. A reference conversion is not a promise that a bank or payment provider will offer that amount. Fees, spreads, settlement timing, and unsupported dates can affect an actual exchange.

bmi-calculator.description: Calculate adult BMI or CDC BMI-for-age percentiles for ages 2 to under 20, with the screening limits of each method explained.

faqs.question: Should a child's BMI use adult categories?
faqs.answer: No. The child mode uses sex-specific CDC references and age in completed months. Adult categories are used from age 20.

faqs.question: Does a BMI result measure body fat or diagnose a condition?
faqs.answer: No. BMI relates weight to height. Body composition, pregnancy and individual health circumstances can limit its interpretation.

sections.title: Choosing an adult or child BMI calculation
paragraphs: BMI relates weight to height, but the adult and child modes do not interpret that number in the same way. Use the age-appropriate mode and check the measurement units before calculating. A BMI category is a screening reference rather than a complete assessment of health or body composition. The result should be considered alongside the limitations and references shown on this page.

anorexic-bmi-calculator.description: Understand adult BMI and why it cannot diagnose anorexia, assess an eating disorder or establish an underweight target.

faqs.question: Can BMI tell me whether someone has anorexia?
faqs.answer: No. Eating disorders can occur at any body size. BMI cannot establish a diagnosis or determine someone's treatment needs.

faqs.question: Why does this page not calculate an anorexic target weight?
faqs.answer: A target based on becoming underweight would misuse the measure. The page provides screening context rather than a weight-loss goal.

sections.title: Why BMI cannot diagnose an eating disorder
paragraphs: This page provides adult BMI information, not a test for anorexia or another eating disorder. A weight-to-height calculation cannot describe eating behaviors, symptoms, or a person's medical needs. Avoid interpreting a category as either a diagnosis or reassurance that no problem exists. If the concern is about eating or health, the relevant next step is an assessment by a qualified health professional.

overweight-calculator.description: Explore adult BMI screening categories from height and weight, with clear limits on what the result can say about individual health.

faqs.question: Does an adult BMI category describe my overall health?
faqs.answer: No. It is a population screening reference. Individual assessment needs more information than weight and height.

faqs.question: Can a muscular person receive a higher BMI category?
faqs.answer: Yes. BMI does not distinguish muscle from fat, so body composition matters when interpreting the number.

sections.title: Interpreting an adult BMI screening category
paragraphs: The calculator uses adult height and weight to produce a BMI screening result. Check the units carefully, especially when switching between metric and imperial measurements. A category does not measure body fat directly or explain why a person's weight has changed. Use the result as one limited piece of information, with the model's notes, rather than as an individualized health target.

bmr-calculator.description: Estimate adult resting energy expenditure using the available equations, and convert food energy between kilocalories and kilojoules.

faqs.question: How is resting energy different from daily maintenance energy?
faqs.answer: Resting energy estimates basic energy expenditure. The activity multiplier produces a broader daily estimate that includes activity assumptions.

faqs.question: Is the equation a measured metabolic rate?
faqs.answer: No. It is a population estimate from body measurements and age, not a direct test of an individual's metabolism.

sections.title: Resting energy versus daily energy needs
paragraphs: A BMR estimate concerns energy used at rest under the selected equation. It should not be confused with a complete daily-energy estimate that also models activity. Check the age, height, weight, and equation inputs before comparing results. The energy-conversion modes answer a separate units question; converting calories and joules does not determine an individual's food or exercise needs.

calorie-calculator.description: Estimate adult daily maintenance calories from body measurements and activity assumptions, with food-energy unit conversion.

faqs.question: Does the displayed calorie estimate prescribe how much I should eat?
faqs.answer: No. It is an adult maintenance-energy estimate. Individual needs can differ, and the model excludes pregnancy, breastfeeding and growing children.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a food Calorie and a kilocalorie?
faqs.answer: They refer to the same food-energy unit. One kilocalorie equals 4.184 kilojoules.

sections.title: Understanding a daily calorie estimate
paragraphs: The daily calorie result combines the selected resting-energy method with an activity assumption. An activity setting describes a modeled average rather than measuring everything done during a day. Compare the assumptions before treating a difference between calculators as an error. The estimate is not a personalized meal prescription, and the displayed limitations explain situations where a simple model is less informative.

tdee-calculator.description: Estimate total daily energy expenditure by combining an adult resting-energy equation with your selected activity factor.

faqs.question: Why does changing activity level change TDEE?
faqs.answer: TDEE multiplies the estimated resting expenditure by an activity factor. The result therefore depends on that activity assumption.

faqs.question: Does TDEE stay constant every day?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. This model gives a single scenario estimate; actual activity, health and other circumstances can change daily expenditure.

sections.title: How activity assumptions affect TDEE
paragraphs: Total daily energy expenditure is an estimate built from the selected body measurements and activity setting. Changing the activity input can substantially change the result even when weight and height stay the same. Use a consistent interpretation of activity when comparing scenarios. This model does not directly measure metabolism or track day-to-day changes in food intake and movement.

macro-calculator.description: Convert a daily energy target into protein, carbohydrate and fat grams, or explore adult reference ranges from body measurements.

faqs.question: Why must my selected macro percentages total 100%?
faqs.answer: Together they allocate the entered energy target. Protein and carbohydrate use about 4 kcal per gram, and fat uses about 9.

faqs.question: Can I combine every upper endpoint of the reference ranges?
faqs.answer: No. The adult reference ranges are independent. Their upper endpoints are not intended to form one 100% dietary split.

sections.title: Connecting macro amounts with an energy target
paragraphs: The macro calculator distributes a stated or estimated energy target into macronutrient amounts. Check whether you are entering calories directly or deriving them from body measurements and activity. A different split can change carbohydrate, fat, and protein grams without changing the total energy target. The output illustrates the selected assumptions and does not assess dietary adequacy or individual medical requirements.

carbohydrate-calculator.description: Estimate carbohydrate grams from a calorie target and percentage, or explore adult energy-based carbohydrate reference ranges.

faqs.question: How are carbohydrate calories converted to grams?
faqs.answer: The model divides energy allocated to carbohydrate by approximately 4 kcal per gram.

faqs.question: Is the calculated carbohydrate amount an individual dietary prescription?
faqs.answer: No. It is a planning quantity or adult reference range, not individualized advice for medical conditions, pregnancy or growing children.

sections.title: Reading carbohydrate grams in context
paragraphs: Carbohydrate grams depend on the energy target and distribution entered in the selected mode. If the target comes from an activity-based estimate, uncertainty in that estimate also affects the carbohydrate result. Compare amounts using the same daily time period. The calculation translates an energy allocation into grams; it does not evaluate food quality, blood-glucose response, or a personal treatment plan.

fat-intake-calculator.description: Convert a selected share of daily calories into fat grams and compare adult energy-based fat-intake reference ranges.

faqs.question: Why does fat produce fewer grams for the same calories?
faqs.answer: The calculation uses about 9 kcal per gram of fat, compared with about 4 for protein or carbohydrate.

faqs.question: Does this tell me which types of dietary fat to choose?
faqs.answer: No. It estimates total fat grams from energy assumptions and does not evaluate food quality or an individual's dietary needs.

sections.title: Understanding an estimated fat allocation
paragraphs: The fat-intake result represents the portion of an energy target assigned to fat by the selected inputs. Check the calorie target before comparing the resulting grams with another scenario. A numerical allocation does not distinguish individual foods or assess the balance of different fatty acids. Use the model's assumptions as context rather than interpreting the result as a complete dietary recommendation.

protein-calculator.description: Estimate daily protein grams from body weight and a chosen g/kg target, or compare adult energy-based protein reference ranges.

faqs.question: What does the grams-per-kilogram target mean?
faqs.answer: It is the daily protein amount assigned to each kilogram of body weight. The calculator multiplies the two values.

faqs.question: Is the default protein target right for everyone?
faqs.answer: No. It reflects the stated adult reference assumption. Activity, age and medical or reproductive circumstances can change individual requirements.

sections.title: Choosing the inputs for a protein estimate
paragraphs: The protein calculator offers a direct daily-protein mode and a mode based on body measurements and activity. Read the selected method before comparing results, because the same label can conceal different assumptions about the calculation base. Check mass units when entering weight. The result is a modeled amount and does not evaluate a person's medical history, diet, or training response.

body-fat-calculator.description: Estimate body-fat percentage using historical circumference equations or the age- and sex-adjusted BMI study model.

faqs.question: Is circumference-based body fat a direct body-composition measurement?
faqs.answer: No. It is an equation-based estimate whose result depends on measurement accuracy and the population assumptions of the method.

faqs.question: Is this the current Army one-site assessment?
faqs.answer: No. The historical Navy circumference equations and the Army one-site equation are different models with different inputs.

faqs.question: Does the BMI estimate measure body fat?
faqs.answer: No. Deurenberg’s equations combine BMI, age and sex statistically. The adult and child equations are separate, and individual error can be several percentage points.

sections.title: Comparing body-fat estimation methods
paragraphs: Circumference-based and BMI-based body-fat methods use different measurements, so their results need not agree. Follow the field instructions and use consistent measurement locations and units. Small input changes can affect a percentage estimate. Neither method directly measures all body tissues, and a difference between the two outputs should not be treated as proof that one is an exact measurement.

army-body-fat-calculator.description: Compare the 2026 Army waist-to-height threshold using recorded measurements, or explore the historical 2023 body-fat equation.

faqs.question: Is waist-to-height ratio a body-fat percentage?
faqs.answer: No. The ratio divides recorded waist circumference by recorded height. The 2026 Army method truncates it to three decimals and compares it with 0.550. The older one-site equation estimates body-fat percentage and is shown separately as historical.

faqs.question: Does this result count as an official assessment?
faqs.answer: No. It calculates from your recorded inputs. Official measurement, confirmation, exemption and administrative procedures require the applicable Army guidance.

sections.title: Selecting the correct Army assessment method
paragraphs: This calculator separates the stated current waist-to-height method from the historical one-site estimate. Select the mode that matches the policy and purpose you are checking before entering measurements. Historical and current outputs should not be compared as if they were the same assessment. Read the source and applicability notes; the calculator does not issue an official fitness or administrative determination.

lean-body-mass-calculator.description: Compare lean-mass estimates from entered body fat, Boer, James, Hume or the pediatric Peters method, with equation-specific limits.

faqs.question: Why can the body-fat and equation methods disagree?
faqs.answer: One subtracts an entered fat fraction from body weight; regression equations infer lean mass from other measurements and population relationships.

faqs.question: Is the pediatric estimate suitable for calculating a medication dose?
faqs.answer: No. The Peters mode is an educational body-composition estimate. Clinical interpretation and medication dosing require a clinician.

sections.title: Understanding lean body mass estimates
paragraphs: Lean body mass is estimated here from either an entered body-fat percentage or a selected reference equation. These approaches can produce different values because they depend on different assumptions. Use the age-appropriate mode and check height and weight units. The output is an estimate of mass outside the modeled fat component, not a direct measurement of skeletal muscle alone.

body-surface-area-calculator.description: Estimate body surface area with eight named equations, age-specific branches and metric or US area units.

faqs.question: What measurements does the Mosteller formula use?
faqs.answer: It takes height in centimeters and weight in kilograms, then calculates the square root of their product divided by 3,600.

faqs.question: Can I use the result to choose a medication dose?
